title: Many prototypes or focus on one idea?
author: Dreamt_Up_Games
selftext: Hi all, wondering how other devs that use AI in the workflows approach this. AI is really good at getting early prototypes of an idea done quickly. But do you all use this to explore several different ideas quickly or do you have one idea in mind and just focus that one down? I’m exploring lots of different ideas but I find it makes it hard to pick and focus down on one I want to take to completion which even with AI still takes a lot of time and effort.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
Depends, is your goal "I want to churn out some popular slop to try to make a quick buck" or are you trying to make a specific game that you *actually want to make*.

That's going to drive your answer.  You can see how many people will post "I made 67 prototypes this month" and it's clear all they're seeing in any of this are hypothetical dollar signs.

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: I just focus on my one idea hoping to make it as good as possible. I’ve been working on it about 7 months and I finally almost have 1 out of 6 floors complete. I don’t really see the point in a shallow prototype since they’re never really fun

comments.author: Shin-Zantesu
comments.body:
Exploration vs Exploitation is an interesting problem in general, my approach is the following: 
Explore as much as possible, aggressively, then focus on one thing only until I can consider it complete, then keep going after that too. 

Exploring and prototyping is fun, Exploitation gets boring quickly, but moving on from exploration is a necessary step that you should take earlier rather than later. It's also cyclical and if you do it well, the results compound: if you explore enough initially, you'll have a good starting point, and if you exploit a lot afterwards, you'll have way more expertise and experience to explore even better in the next round. The Optimal Stopping Solution suggests that it's optimal to stop exploration at 37% of the way, if you can somehow measure how much the whole (100%) is. I'd suggest you set yourself deadlines.

comments.author: Coindk
comments.body:
I always start working on 10 ideas at the same time and work on the one I want to go with at any given time, if I have an eleventh one popping in my yead I add it to a "coming next" list.I simply don't touch it until one of the 10 is done with. 

This allowed me to work more, with more motivation, with more pleasure and far less downtimes than starting just one project and stick to it.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
One project that is the one I want to make.

Considering the work left to be done I will have a few months with just this one.

comments.author: theprupletrainer
comments.body:
I assume you want to complete a game you will be satisfied with. 100+ prototypes can leave you with choice paralysis.

You have to know what you want. Take a core game loop you like, stick to it, build on top of it and make it fun. Finish the game. Note down what worked and what didn’t, then make your next move.

comments.author: damnthewizard
comments.body:
I recommend a prototype for each type of gameplay. Like a combat prototype, economy prototype, team manager prototype. 

Once each of these has been iterated on then you can bring them to gather together fairly and iterate on the larger combine led gameplay.

comments.author: RecordingTechnical86
comments.body: create many prototypes until you have one thats genuinly fun. Then let someone else play it and decide if thats the one you want to focus on

comments.author: fluxtah
comments.body: Build your dream game or chase the money, exploring lots of ideas sounds like you don't have anything or your doing it for the wrong reasons, though tell me that I am wrong 😄

comments.author: Den_er_da_hvid
comments.body: I usually have one game idea I workon. I quickly get a prototype and then iterate on that til I accept that it is not a good idea that can carry a whole game.

comments.author: algorys
comments.body:
Une idée !

Perso, je me concentre sur 1 idée et je développe 1 jeu à la fois.

Par contre de temps en temps pour me faire plaisir je fais des prototypes pour voir :)

comments.author: DudeWithASweater
comments.body: I explored about a dozen prototypes before I landed on one that actually felt like it had legs. Since then I've been going deep on this one game.
